title: Dos & don'ts
slide_intent: Teach a partner to choose the identifier that describes the relationship accurately. A viewer should be able to tell whose channel they are visiting and when Frontline AIDS shares responsibility for a project.
strategic_value: The partner stamp can signal affiliation while leaving the host organization identifiable. A masterbrand lockup can name Frontline AIDS where it has a direct role.
demonstration: Five annotated website and social examples compare the partner stamp on a header or footer with uses of the masterbrand on joint work and partner lists. Pink notes flag unsuitable placements.
practical_value: Use the stamp in a partner’s visible header or footer. For a joint project or list of partner organizations, use the masterbrand alongside the other names.

content_islands.name: Section rail and heading
content_islands.spec: Mark Dos & Don'ts under the partner-stamp section. Place the partner badge kicker above the heading.

content_islands.name: Stamp placements
content_islands.spec: Arrange the social header, website header and footer across the first row. Pair each image with short allowed and disallowed treatments.

content_islands.name: Masterbrand placements
content_islands.spec: Place the joint project and partner list in the lower row. Match the notes to the examples so the reader can distinguish the two marks’ roles.
